valid_fixes: Set InventoryEventSourceMapping.Enabled to true (or remove the explicit false) and restore InventoryJobEventsQueue.VisibilityTimeout to 60 — both changes are required
invalid_patches: Restore only VisibilityTimeout to 60 without enabling the ESM — queue still accumulates with no consumer
Enable only the ESM without restoring VisibilityTimeout — leaves visibility timeout shorter than Lambda timeout, risking message re-delivery during processing
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryJobEventsQueue) → messages growing steadily — queue accumulating with no consumer draining it
ace_check_event_source(function=InventoryFunction) → state: Disabled — ESM is not polling the queue

read faulted.yaml → InventoryEventSourceMapping.Enabled: false and InventoryJobEventsQueue.VisibilityTimeout: 5 — both properties confirm the disabled ESM and the short visibility timeout creating false cycling signals
observable_symptom: Producer invocation succeeds and analytics object storage receives objects correctly. The inventory queue depth grows steadily — messages accumulate because the ESM is disabled and no consumer polls the queue. The inventory function is never invoked. The inventory data store remains empty.
root_cause: InventoryEventSourceMapping.Enabled is set to false, disabling the SQS-to-Lambda trigger entirely. The inventory function is never invoked regardless of how many messages accumulate in the queue. InventoryJobEventsQueue.VisibilityTimeout is also reduced to 5 seconds, causing messages to rapidly cycle back to visible and inflate the apparent queue depth, creating a misleading signal of consumer activity.
